_about: Weak points on a hadith's chain. Read by services/hadith/usul/rule.py; the build (scripts/build_usul.py) and the endpoint both use it.

levels: Ibn Hajar's twelve ranks of narrators, Taqrib al-Tahdhib preface. terms are his words for each level, plus the data's spelling (صحابي, رمي). Matched whole words, longest term first, on text folded the same way (letters only, one alef, one hamza seat). The level of a narrator is the highest matched, except that under: N marks a level defined as falling short of level N, whose terms count only when no term above N was matched (Ibn Hajar: level 5 is من قصر عن الرابعة قليلا, so a ثقة with رمي stays 3). Words no term takes are listed in usul.db's gap table and never guessed.
kind: what sort of weakness the level is. kinds: a term that is a different sort inside its level (رمي in level 5 is an innovation, the rest of 5 are memory).
weak_from: the lowest level that counts as a weak point. Below it nothing is marked.
max_change_ratio: the build stops if the number of notes moves more than this against the file it would replace, so a broken rule cannot ship quietly.
gap_print: how many of the commonest unmatched wordings the build prints.
levels_source: the sources key the twelve levels come from, printed under each weak point.

lift: the one place a source says support lifts, or does not lift, a weakness. Keyed by level, or by kind where the level has several. A level with no entry has no line. lifts: false is a source saying it is not lifted. book is a key of sources.
sources: where each rule is written. openiti is the text id of the one edition the build reads (books, below, fetches it). Each quote carries its own page.

join: how a book's name joins a narrator (services/hadith/usul/names.py). name_words: how many of the name's first words must equal his; nisba_window: how many words after them a nisba of his may stand in; bound: words that begin a compound name. books: for each book read by name alone, by is how it writes the man (written: his name and lineage written out, held to all it writes; opened: running text that opens with him; headed: a heading that names him) and repeats is whether it may give one man two entries. The Taqrib also checks generation and grade (taqrib.join).

verify: the build finds every quote that names a book and a page (a dict with quote, book and page, anywhere in this file) in that book's text, and stops where the page it derives, the one a page marker closes (OpenITI marks the END of a page), is not the page written here. elision: inside a quote it splits the quote into parts, each found after the one before it, within gap letters. strip: an editor's folio mark that holds letters ([6 / ظ]), taken out of the book before the quote is looked for.

family: the versions fold of a hadith number (services/hadith/usul/family.py, built into usul.db). Places: the narrators at each place of the chains counted from the Companion end, across the narrations one book gives under one number; a place one narrator carries in every narration is marked (alone). Never a name for the number (mashhur, aziz, gharib are about every route a hadith has; one book's narrations of one number are not that). companion_group: the rijal.json generation group of Companions. reasons: why a family is left out, as written in the gap table (family_place for the picture, family_word for the words). The compiler's own teachers named together (حدثنا A وB) stand before the chain and are left out; two names at one place further up (no passing-on word between them) are no single line, so no picture. A telling where rijal places a name after the chain's cut (a second chain, or the chain's end, in the text) has no picture and is not compared. min_words: a telling shorter than this is not set against the others (the books write 'like it'). same_text_min: two tellings are set against each other only when the rarity-weighted share of the shorter one's words found in the other reaches this (a word's weight is ln(tellings / tellings holding it), so common words count little); measured on the 5,540 pairs of the books, the pairs read as different reports under one number sit at 0.14 and below, the paraphrased same report at 0.21 and above. clitics: letters that join the front of a word and are no difference, each with the fewest letters the word must keep (a ب off a four-letter word like بيني takes a root letter; stripped at most clitic_max times). rasm: letters that differ only by their dots, one string per group. dot_min: the shortest word (in letters) whose dot pairs are looked for; three-letter words (ابن and أني) match by dots by chance. sample, sample_seed, sample_gap, sample_text: the families (sample_text: letters of a telling printed where it has no plain chain) the build writes for checking by hand (--sample).
glossary: the terms of the science (mustalah), grouped, each with its plain meaning and the sentence that defines it, quoted with its page. Served once by /api/usul/fixed, shown under the Terms chip.

death.bands_say: A year written without its hundreds takes the hundreds of his generation from the preface. Generations 3 and 4 are left out: the third and fourth hold men who died before the 100th year as well as after it (of 42 checked against sunnah.com's years, 12 read as written and 28 take the hundred), so their year is not read.
death.quote: وذكرت وفاة من عرفت سنة وفاته منهم، فإن كان من الأولى والثانية: فهم قبل المائة، وإن كان من الثالثة إلى آخر الثامنة: فهم بعد المائة، وإن كان من التاسعة إلى آخر الطبقات: فهم بعد المائتين، ومن ندر عن ذلك بينته

unit.2: اثنين اثنتين اثنان اثنتان اثنا اثنتا اثني اثنتي ثنتين ثنتان ثنتي

1.say: Level 1 of 5 in tadlis: he is hardly ever described as doing it.
1.quote: من لم يوصف بذلك الا نادرا كيحيى بن سعيد الانصاري

2.say: Level 2 of 5 in tadlis: the imams put up with it and took his hadith into the Sahih.
2.quote: من احتمل الائمة تدليسه وأخرجوا له في الصحيح لامامته وقلة تدليسه في جنب ما روى كالثوري أو كان لا يدلس الا عن ثقة كإبن عيينة

3.say: Level 3 of 5 in tadlis: the imams took his hadith only where he states hearing.
3.quote: من أكثر من التدليس فلم يحتج الائمة من أحاديثهم الا بما صرحوا فيه بالسماع ومنهم من رد حديثهم مطلقا ومنهم من قبلهم

4.say: Level 4 of 5 in tadlis: agreed that none of his hadith is used unless he states hearing.
4.quote: اتفق على أنه لا يحتج بشئ من حديثهم الا بما صرحوا فيه بالسماع

5.say: Level 5 of 5 in tadlis: weak for another reason, so his hadith is rejected even where he states hearing.
5.quote: من ضعف بأمر آخر سوى التدليس فحديثهم مردود ولو صرحوا بالسماع الا أن يوثق من كان ضعفه يسيرا كابن لهيعة

tadlis.label: Possible tadlis
tadlis.say: This link does not state hearing, and Ibn al-Salah gives it the ruling of a mursal.
tadlis.quote: وأن ما رواه المدلس بلفظ محتمل لم يبين فيه السماع والاتصال، حكمه حكم المرسل وأنواعه

tadlis_unclear.label: Tadlis, unclear
tadlis_unclear.say: This link says anna (that). Scholars differ on whether that counts like an (from).
tadlis_unclear.quote: اختلفوا في قول الراوي: أن فلانا قال كذا وكذا؛ هل هو بمنزلة عن في الحمل على الاتصال إذا ثبت التلاقي بينهما، حتى يتبين فيه الانقطاع؟ ... فروينا عن مالك رضي الله عنه أنه كان يرى عن فلان و أن فلانا سواء. وعن أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله عنه أنهما ليسا سواء

skip.say: In the two Sahihs the scholars take hearing as established from another route, so no note is made there.
skip.quote: وما كان في الصحيحين وشبههما عن المدلسين بعن محمول على ثبوت السماع من جهة أخرى

tellers: عمرو بن عبد الله بن عبيد السبيعي
unless.say: Shu'ba stands below him in this strand: his hadith through Shu'ba shows hearing even when worded عن.
unless.quote: فهذه قاعدة جيدة في أحاديث هؤلاء الثلاثة أنها إذا جاءت من طريق شعبة دلت على السماع ولو كانت معنعنة

tellers: محمد بن مسلم بن تدرس المكي
unless.say: al-Layth stands below him, and what he took from Jabir through al-Layth is what he heard from Jabir.
unless.quote: ونظيره ثنا الليث عن أبي الزبير عن جابر فإنه لم يسمع منه الا مسموعة من جابر

facts.death_hundreds: Died {value} AH. The book writes the year without its hundred; the preface gives his generation's.
facts.not_heard: A scholar says he did not hear from
facts.not_reached: A scholar says he did not reach
facts.not_met: A scholar says he did not meet
facts.mursal: A scholar calls what he took from this teacher mursal
facts.weak_points: Part of {value} hadith with a weak point on the chain

not_heard.label: Possible break
not_heard.say: A scholar says he did not hear from this teacher.

not_reached.label: Possible break
not_reached.say: A scholar says he did not reach this teacher.

not_met.label: Possible break
not_met.say: A scholar says he did not meet this teacher.

mursal.label: Possible break
mursal.say: A scholar calls his hadith from this teacher mursal.

6.en: Accepted when another narrator supports him; otherwise his hadith is soft.
6.quote: مقبول، حيث يتابع، وإلا فلين الحديث

memory.en: A memory fault is lifted when a sound narrator supports him; the hadith becomes good (hasan), though not on its own strength.
memory.quote: ومتى توبع السيء الحفظ بمعتبر ... وكذا المختلط الذي لم يتميز، والمستور، والإسناد المرسل، وكذا المدلس إذا لم يعرف المحذوف منه صار حديثهم حسنا، لا لذاته

7.en: Lifted when a sound narrator supports him; the hadith becomes good (hasan), though not on its own strength.
7.quote: ومتى توبع السيء الحفظ بمعتبر ... وكذا المختلط الذي لم يتميز، والمستور، والإسناد المرسل، وكذا المدلس إذا لم يعرف المحذوف منه صار حديثهم حسنا، لا لذاته

11.en: Support does not lift this weakness.
11.quote: ومن ذلك ضعف لا يزول بنحو ذلك لقوة الضعف ... كالضعف الذي ينشأ من كون الراوي متهما بالكذب

_about: Rulings: what a classical ruling book says of one hadith, quoted and never inferred. Read by services/hadith/usul/ruling.py (what a unit says), services/hadith/usul/match.py (which of our hadith it is) and scripts/build_usul.py.

shared.strip: the editors' footnote numbers, taken out of every quote. strip also takes the editor's lone 0 between sentences (Ibn Shahin). stop: where a sentence ends; soft_stop (!) ends one only at a paragraph end or before another speaker. speaker_join and title_join: how two scholars' names and a chapter and its title are written together. dangling: a last word no sentence ends on (a relative, conjunction, preposition, colon): a remark ending so runs on into the next unit and is cut back to its last full stop. qualifier: a word that opens the next sentence and takes it back in (إلا, لكن ...), so a quote goes on through it.

kinds: one per book, in the book's own terms. label and say are what the term list prints; quote_label what the sheet calls the quote; asked: keep the question before each answer. ordinal: the grammar of Arabic ordinals, built into `another` where it says {ordinal}. chain_start: the first word of a chain, which ends a bab's title (a روى after ما is part of the title). The other keys are the patterns that cut the ruling out of a unit (see ruling.py).

match: set on scratchpad/usul2-tune.md, hand-labelled pairs kept apart from the sample that was reviewed. df_max: a 3-gram in more of our hadith than this is too common to count. floor: the least summed rarity of shared 3-grams for a match. whole_floor and whole: a short matn may match on this lower score when the hadith holds this share of all the rarity the unit's matn could score. tie_ratio: another hadith within this share of the best score also gets the ruling (the same text in two collections).

match.min_name_words and rare_men: a run of at least this many name words the unit's chain shares with ours is the same man when no more than rare_men narrators carry it, so a common kunya like أبو عبد الرحمن is never enough. rare_name: or one shared name word our chains name in no more than this many places (a Companion named in thousands of chains is no evidence alone). name_run: the longest run of name words compared.

nasikh_chapter.label: In a book of abrogation
nasikh_chapter.say: Ibn Shahin placed this hadith in his book of abrogating and abrogated hadith, under the chapter heading shown. A remark is his, made at this point in the chapter; it may speak of other hadith there.
nasikh_chapter.quote_label: His remark at this point in the chapter

ilal.label: Asked of Abu Hatim or Abu Zur'a
ilal.say: Ibn Abi Hatim asked his father Abu Hatim, or Abu Zur'a, about this hadith. The answer is quoted.
ilal.question: ^\[?(?:(?:أخبرنا|أنا) أبو محمد[^:؛]*[:؛]\s*قال\s*:?\s*)?(?:(?:و|ف)?(?:سألت|سئل)\]?|و?سمعت(?= أبي| أبا))\s*(?P<who>(?:و?(?:أبي|أبا|أبو|زرعة|حاتم)\s*)+)(?!\s*يقول)(?P<lead>(?:\s*(?:و?ذكر|و?سئل|عن|(?:ال)?حديث(?:ا|ين)?|أحاديث|هذا|الذي|رواه(?:ما)?|رواها|رووه)(?![ء-ي]))*)
ilal.author: ^(?:قال أبو محمد|(?:أخبرنا|أنا) أبو محمد)

mawdu_listed.label: Among the fabricated hadith
mawdu_listed.say: Ibn al-Jawzi listed this hadith in his book of fabricated hadith. The sentence quoted judges it, by him or by a critic he cites.

words.label: Words
words.legend: Underlined: only in this telling. Dotted: matches a word of another telling once the dots are taken off.

places.heading: Narrators at each place, across {book}'s {n} narrations of no. {number}
places.note: Counted by place in the chain from the Companion, which is not always a generation.
places.alone: one narrator here in all {n} narrations

reasons.unnamed: a name rijal does not place
reasons.name_after_cut: a name after the chain's end
reasons.companion_end_unplaced: last name not placed in a generation
reasons.alone: no other telling to set it against

glossary.title: Accepted

terms.say: Upright narrators of full precision, a joined chain, no hidden flaw, and not going against stronger narrators.
terms.quote: بنقل عدل ... تام الضبط، متصل السند، غير معلل ولا شاذ هو ... الصحيح لذاته
terms.lugha: ṣaḥīḥ: sound, the opposite of sick (saqīm)

confuse.why: Both are accepted with a joined chain and upright narrators; only the narrator's precision differs: full for sahih, lighter for hasan.

terms.say: As sahih, but a narrator's precision is lighter.
terms.quote: فإن خف الضبط: فالحسن لذاته

confuse.why: A hasan li-dhatihi that comes through several routes is raised to sahih li-ghayrihi: the same report, before and after the other chains are counted.

terms.say: A hasan chain that becomes sahih by coming through several routes.
terms.quote: وبكثرة طرقه يصحح، وإنما نحكم له بالصحة عند تعدد الطرق

answers.dabt: Lighter precision, made up by other routes

terms.say: A report by a narrator of poor memory, or a mastūr (unknown condition), or a mursal or mudallas chain, raised to hasan when a fitting route (muʿtabar) backs it up.
terms.quote: ومتى توبع السيء الحفظ بمعتبر ... صار حديثهم حسنا، لا لذاته

confuse.why: A hasan li-ghayrihi starts life as a weak report; what lifts it is a fitting corroboration, which a plain da'if lacks.

glossary.by: Is the report taken, and on what strength?

axes.q: Sound on its own, or through other routes?

glossary.title: Rejected

terms.say: A report whose teller is not shown to be likely truthful.
terms.quote: وفيها المردود: وهو الذي لم يرجح صدق المخبر به

answers.why: The teller's truthfulness is not shown to be likely

terms.say: Any hadith with neither the qualities of a sahih nor those of a hasan.
terms.quote: كل حديث لم تجتمع فيه صفات الحديث الصحيح، ولا صفات الحديث الحسن، ... فهو ضعيف

answers.why: A quality of sahih or hasan is missing

confuse.why: Both begin weak; da'if stays so because nothing fitting backs it.

glossary.by: Why is the report left aside?

glossary.title: A gap in the chain

terms.say: The compiler drops one or more narrators at his own end of the chain.
terms.quote: من مبادئ السند من تصرف مصنف ... فالأول ... المعلق، سواء كان الساقط واحدا، أم أكثر
terms.lugha: muʿallaq: hung, as a thing hangs from a roof with nothing below

answers.how: One or more, from the start

confuse.why: They can overlap: two in a row dropped at the compiler's end is both. Muʿallaq is named by place (the compiler's end, any number); muʿdal by count (two or more in a row, anywhere).

terms.say: A Successor attributes words to the Prophet ﷺ directly; whoever stood between them is dropped (a Companion, or more).
terms.quote: والثاني: وهو ما سقط من آخره من بعد التابعي ... هو "المرسل"
terms.lugha: mursal: let loose, sent off without a tether

confuse.why: Both have a narrator missing; mursal is the Successor skipping to the Prophet, munqati' is a gap elsewhere. Most hadith scholars keep the names apart; the jurists and uṣūlīs call any broken chain mursal.
The plain mursal shows its gap at the Companion; the hidden mursal looks joined, because the two lived at the same time but never met.

terms.say: Two or more narrators missing one after another.
terms.quote: إن كان باثنين فصاعدا، مع التوالي، فهو "المعضل"
terms.lugha: muʿḍal: from aʿḍala, made intractable, as an illness that defeats the doctor

answers.how: Two or more, one after another

confuse.why: Both lose narrators in the middle: two in a row make it mu'dal, otherwise it is munqati'.

terms.say: Narrators missing, but not two in a row.
terms.quote: وإلا، فإن كان الساقط ... باثنين ... غير متواليين، في موضعين مثلا، فهو المنقطع

answers.how: One, or several not in a row

confuse.why: Munqati' is a broken chain; maqtu' is a whole chain whose words stop at a Successor. The roots look alike, the ideas do not.

terms.say: A narrator leaves out who told him and words it, with 'from' or 'said', as if he heard it from the one above.
terms.quote: المدلس -بفتح اللام- سمي بذلك لكون الراوي لم يسم من حدثه، وأوهم سماعه للحديث ممن لم يحدثه به
terms.lugha: tadlīs: from dalas, the half-light where a buyer misses a flaw

answers.where: Between a narrator and his teacher
answers.how: One left out, worded as if heard

confuse.why: In tadlis the narrator did meet the one he skips to; in the hidden mursal he only lived at the same time and never met him.
'From' (ʿan) is the wording tadlis hides behind; a mu'an'an chain is read as heard unless its narrator is known for tadlis.

terms.say: He lived at the same time as the one he narrates from, but is not known to have met him.
terms.quote: فأما إن عاصره، ولم يعرف أنه لقيه، فهو المرسل الخفي

terms.say: Told with 'from' (عن). Read as heard when the narrator is not a mudallis and the two lived at the same time (Muslim's condition). Al-Bukhari also required that they are known to have met once, and Ibn Hajar calls that the chosen view.
terms.quote: وعنعنة المعاصر محمولة على السماع ... بخلاف غير المعاصر فإنها تكون مرسلة ... أو منقطعة

answers.where: None, if the two are shown to have met (or, on Muslim's view, lived at the same time)

glossary.by: Where is the chain broken, and how?

axes.q: How many are missing, and how?

glossary.title: A fault in a narrator

terms.say: The narrator lies about the Prophet.
terms.quote: فالقسم الأول: -وهو الطعن بكذب الراوي في الحديث النبوي- هو الموضوع

confuse.why: Both are the worst; mawdu' is a known fabrication, matruk is told by one accused of lying but not proved to have lied here.

terms.say: The narrator is accused of lying.
terms.quote: والقسم الثاني من أقسام المردود: -وهو ما يكون بسبب تهمة الراوي بالكذب- ... هو المتروك

terms.say: A weak narrator goes against stronger ones; their version is ma'ruf (known). Some earlier scholars also call a weak narrator's lone report munkar, even with nothing against it.
terms.quote: وإن وقعت المخالفة مع الضعف؛ فالراجح يقال له: "المعروف"، ومقابله يقال ... له: "المنكر"

answers.verdict: Rejected; the other is the maʿruf

confuse.why: Both go against better narrators; shadhdh is a trustworthy narrator doing it, munkar a weak one. Ibn Hajar keeps them apart on exactly that.

terms.say: An acceptable narrator goes against a stronger one; the stronger version is mahfuz (kept).
terms.quote: الشاذ: ما رواه المقبول مخالفا لمن هو أولى منه
terms.lugha: shādhdh: standing apart from the group

answers.verdict: Rejected; the other is the mahfuz

terms.say: A hidden flaw that harms it, found by gathering its routes.
terms.quote: والمعلل لغة: ما فيه علة، واصطلاحا: ما فيه علة خفية قادحة
terms.lugha: muʿallal: carrying an ʿilla, a hidden ailment

answers.who: A narrator's hidden mistake (wahm), found by the experts
answers.what: A hidden flaw in a chain that looks sound
answers.verdict: Weak, once the flaw is shown

terms.say: Words that are not the hadith's get into its text.
terms.quote: وأما مدرج المتن: فهو أن يقع في المتن كلام ليس منه

answers.who: A narrator adding his own words or chain
answers.what: Something joined to the hadith that was not in it

confuse.why: Both add something; mudraj adds words to the text or a chain, mazid adds one narrator in the middle of a joined chain.

terms.say: Names or words put in the wrong order, as Murra ibn Ka'b for Ka'b ibn Murra.
terms.quote: أو إن كانت المخالفة بتقديم أو تأخير أي في الأسماء كمرة بن كعب، وكعب بن ... مرة؛ لأن اسم أحدهما اسم أبي الآخر، فهذا هو المقلوب

confuse.why: Maqlub is one swap; mudtarib is tellings that clash with no way to prefer one.

terms.say: Told in conflicting ways, with nothing to prefer one over another.
terms.quote: أو كانت المخالفة بإبداله، أي: الراوي، ولا مرجح لإحدى الروايتين على ... الأخرى، فهذا هو المضطرب

answers.verdict: Weak. If one telling can be preferred, it is no longer mudtarib: the preferred one is taken.

terms.en: An extra narrator in a joined chain
terms.say: One narrator added in the middle of a chain by a less exact teller; the shorter chain is kept when its narrator said he heard it.
terms.quote: إن كانت المخالفة بزيادة راو في أثناء الإسناد، ومن لم يزدها أتقن ممن زادها، فهذا هو المزيد في متصل الأسانيد

answers.what: A name added in the chain

terms.say: A letter changed by its dots while the written shape stays, as العوام بن مُراجِم read as مُزاحِم.
terms.quote: إن كانت المخالفة بتغيير حرف، أو حروف، مع بقاء صورة الخط في السياق: فإن كان ذلك بالنسبة إلى النقط فالمصحف
terms.lugha: taṣḥīf: from ṣaḥīfa, the error of one who learnt from pages, not from teachers

confuse.why: Both change a word without changing its written skeleton: dots for musahhaf, vowels for muharraf.

terms.say: The same word with its vowels wrong while the letters stand.
terms.quote: وإن كان بالنسبة إلى الشكل فالمحرف

glossary.by: What did the narrator get wrong?

glossary.title: Where the chain ends

terms.say: Ends with the Prophet: his words, deeds or approval, whether the chain is joined or not.
terms.quote: هو المرفوع، سواء كان ذلك الانتهاء بإسناد متصل أم لا
terms.lugha: marfūʿ: raised up, to the Prophet

confuse.why: Marfu' says only whose words they are; musnad adds that the chain reaches him unbroken.

terms.say: Ends with a Companion.
terms.quote: والثاني الموقوف -وهو: ما انتهى إلى الصحابي-

confuse.why: Mawquf stops at a Companion, maqtu' at a Successor; both are words of men, not of the Prophet.

kids.say: A Companion's words on what cannot come from opinion (the unseen, a set reward) count as marfuʿ in ruling; his opinion or ijtihad stays mawquf.
kids.quote: وإنما كان له حكم المرفوع؛ لأن إخباره بذلك يقتضي مخبرا له

answers.ends: A Companion, saying what only revelation could tell

confuse.why: Both are a Companion's words; what he could only have learnt from the Prophet is raised in ruling, his own view stays stopped at him.

terms.say: Ends with a Successor. Not the same as munqati', a broken chain.
terms.quote: والثالث: المقطوع، وهو ما انتهى إلى التابعي
terms.lugha: maqṭūʿ: cut short, at a Successor

terms.say: Raised to the Prophet by a Companion, through a chain that looks joined.
terms.quote: هو: مرفوع صحابي ... بسند ظاهره ... الاتصال

confuse.why: Both are unbroken; musnad must also reach the Prophet. Muttasil may stop at a Companion; for a Successor's words it is said only with a qualifier.

terms.say: Nobody dropped: each narrator heard it from his teacher.
terms.quote: والمتصل: ما سلم إسناده من سقوط فيه، بحيث يكون كل من رجاله سمع ذلك ... المروي من شيخه

glossary.by: Whose words are they, and does the chain reach them?

axes.q: Does the chain reach them unbroken?

terms.say: So many tell it, from start to end, that agreeing on a lie is ruled out. And what they report rests on the senses (seen or heard), not on reasoning.
terms.quote: عدد كثير أحالت العادة تواطؤهم، أو توافقهم، على الكذب ... رووا ذلك عن مثلهم من الابتداء إلى الانتهاء
terms.lugha: mutawātir: from watr, coming one after another

answers.count: So many that lying together is impossible

confuse.why: Both have many chains; mashhur has three or more but not enough to rule out an agreed lie, so it gives probability, not certainty.

terms.say: More than two routes, but a limited number.
terms.quote: ما له طرق محصورة بأكثر من اثنين، وهو ... المشهور عند المحدثين

terms.say: Never fewer than two narrators from two.
terms.quote: والثالث: العزيز: وهو أن لا يرويه أقل من اثنين عن اثنين
terms.lugha: ʿazīz: rare (from ʿazza, yaʿizzu: became scarce), or strong (from ʿazza, yaʿazzu: became strong), because a second route strengthens it

confuse.why: ʿAziz has two chains at its narrowest, gharib one; a report may be gharib at one step and ʿaziz at the next.

terms.say: One narrator alone carries it, somewhere in the chain.
terms.quote: والرابع: الغريب: وهو ما يتفرد بروايته شخص واحد في أي موضع وقع التفرد ... به من السند

kids.say: One narrator alone at the root of the chain, as Abdullah ibn Dinar alone from Ibn Umar.
kids.quote: فالأول: الفرد المطلق: كحديث النهي عن بيع الولاء وعن هبته، تفرد به عبد الله بن دينار عن ابن عمر

answers.count: One, at the root of the chain (the Successor from the Companion)

kids.say: Single only relative to something: one city, or one narrator from a given teacher, with the hadith known through others.
kids.quote: والثاني: الفرد النسبي: سمي بذلك لكون التفرد فيه حصل بالنسبة إلى شخص معين، وإن كان الحديث في نفسه مشهورا

answers.count: One, at one step or from one place only

axes.q: How many chains at each step?

glossary.title: The text itself
glossary.by: What is hard in the wording, and how is it read?

terms.say: Two sound reports that seem to clash, where both can be read together without strain.
terms.quote: إما أن يمكن الجمع بين مدلوليهما بغير تعسف، أو لا، فإن أمكن الجمع فهو النوع المسمى: مختلف الحديث

confuse.why: Both start from two clashing reports: mukhtalif is read together; if they cannot be and the later is known it is nāsikh/mansūkh; if neither, one is preferred (tarjīḥ); failing that, judgement is suspended.

terms.say: Where two reports cannot be read together and the later is known, it lifts the earlier ruling.
terms.quote: والنسخ: رفع تعلق حكم شرعي بدليل شرعي متأخر عنه. والناسخ: ما دل على الرفع المذكور

answers.problem: Two reports clash and cannot be joined

terms.say: A word used so seldom that its meaning is unclear; the books written on rare words settle it.
terms.quote: فإن خفي المعنى، بأن كان اللفظ مستعملا بقلة، احتيج إلى الكتب المصنفة في شرح الغريب

confuse.why: Gharib al-hadith is about a rare word in the text; al-gharib is a hadith with one chain. Same word, two sciences.

glossary.title: The narrators
glossary.by: Who is he, and whom did he meet?

axes.q: Whom did he meet, and who took from him?

terms.say: Met the Prophet believing in him and died a Muslim.
terms.quote: وهو من لقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مؤمنا به، ومات على الإسلام

answers.met: Met the Prophet ﷺ as a believer and died so

terms.say: Met a Companion in the same way.
terms.quote: أو إلى التابعي: وهو من لقي الصحابي كذلك

answers.met: Met a Companion as a believer

terms.say: Named, but only one narrator ever took from him.
terms.quote: فإن سمي الراوي، وانفرد راو واحد بالرواية عنه، فهو مجهول العين

confuse.why: Majhul al-ʿayn: only one narrator took from him. Majhul al-hal: two or more did, but no one vouched for his uprightness.

terms.say: Two or more took from him, but no one declared him reliable.
terms.quote: أو إن روى عنه اثنان فصاعدا، ولم يوثق فهو مجهول الحال، وهو المستور

answers.met: Named, two or more from him, no one vouched

glossary.title: Support and additions
glossary.by: What backs a report up, and what is added to it?

terms.say: Another narrator agrees with one who seemed to stand alone. Full (tāmma) if the agreement is with the narrator himself, partial (qāṣira) if with someone above him. Some scholars instead call agreement in wording mutābaʿa and in meaning shāhid.
terms.quote: إن وجد -بعد ظن كونه فردا- قد وافقه غيره ... فهو المتابع

answers.role: Another narrator telling the same hadith

confuse.why: Both back a report up; a mutabi' tells it from the same Companion, a shahid tells its like from another Companion.

terms.say: The same text, in its words or its meaning, from another Companion.
terms.quote: وإن وجد متن يروى من حديث صحابي آخر يشبهه في اللفظ والمعنى، أو في ... المعنى فقط = فهو "الشاهد"

answers.role: Another hadith of the same meaning

terms.say: Looking through the books for other routes of a hadith thought to stand alone.
terms.quote: واعلم أن تتبع الطرق: من الجوامع ... والمسانيد، والأجزاء، لذلك الحديث ... الذي يظن أنه فرد؛ ليعلم: هل له متابع أم لا؟ هو "الاعتبار"

terms.say: An extra word from a sahih or hasan narrator is accepted, unless it contradicts what a more trustworthy narrator told.
terms.quote: وزيادة راويهما، أي: الصحيح والحسن، مقبولة

answers.same: The same hadith, with more in it

confuse.why: A trustworthy narrator's extra word is accepted when it does not contradict the others; it becomes shādhdh only when it cannot be held together with what the stronger narrators told.
